Integrated assessment with Beige Book reference:
- FOMC stance (Mar 15, 2020): Emergency move to the ELB (0–0.25%), large-scale purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS, expanded repos, discount window cut, and coordinated USD swap lines. This is a strong policy backstop aimed at supporting market functioning, credit flows, and the outlook amid COVID-19 shocks. Inflation below 2% and energy sector under stress add urgency.
- Beige Book lens: District reports ahead of mid-March showed modest overall growth but rising headwinds. Coronavirus was cited as a key risk; travel and tourism softened; manufacturing faced supply-chain strains; natural resource extraction/energy weakened; transportation activity was uneven (with isolated strength at some ports); consumer spending and nonresidential real estate/leasing varied across districts; agricultural conditions were little changed; labor markets were tight but constrained; pricing pressures were muted. Loan growth was impacted, with indications of emerging caution but not yet a collapse.
- SLOOS overlay: Banks tightened standards (especially C&I and construction/land development), raised credit thresholds/trimmed limits, and reported weaker loan demand in several segments. They expected further tightening, reduced risk tolerance, and deterioration in portfolios, collateral values, and HELOCs—signaling a contractionary credit channel that can blunt policy transmission.
- Net: Powerful policy easing and liquidity support are meaningful mitigants, but Beige Book evidence of sectoral softening and SLOOS-confirmed tightening in credit conditions tilt the outlook negative. Mixed district activity and still-modest inflation temper the downside somewhat.
